A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same alternating-MoE multimodal alignment work, renamed from Alt-MoE to M3-Jepa. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval, image-classification, VQA/NLVR-2, ablation and efficiency results in its main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark and ablation results and reports a revised loss-weight sensitivity experiment. Results retained from v2 remain original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The alternating MoE, modality/task embeddings, prediction loss and contrastive loss are retained; v2 already investigated loss weighting. However, v4 Sections 4.1/4.4 newly describe one-hot labels as a modality, while Appendix B.3 retains v2's frozen DINOv2/CLIP fusion and linear-probing description. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a procedural adaptation or a reinterpretation of unchanged experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions cover COCO/Flickr30K retrieval, zero-shot Clotho/AudioCaps retrieval, ImageNet-1K classification and VQAv2/NLVR-2. The audio-training combinations involving WavText5K and Freesound are also retained. Label-modality and mixed-input framing does not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: ONE-PEACE appears in v2's supplementary VQA/NLVR-2 Table 1 but is omitted from the corresponding v4 Table 4, although Appendix B.4 still discusses it. The matched retrieval and classification comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The loss-sensitivity protocol changes: v2 Appendix 1.3 plots separate prediction/contrastive weights over 0.4–1.0 using Average Recall@1, whereas v4 Section 4.6 uses complementary weights alpha and 1-alpha over 0–1 and specifies COCO text-to-image R@1. These are differently specified experiments, not a same-setting performance comparison.

E4.justification: v2 Section 5.6's prediction-representation retrieval ablation, comparing prediction-only with joint training, is removed. The earlier two-curve loss-weight analysis is replaced by v4's alpha sensitivity study. MoE/MLP, alternating-training and LoRA ablations, routing-schedule comparisons, efficiency analysis and the similarity-matrix example are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals, error bars or significance tests. v4's reference to averaged retrieval time does not introduce a documented uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Most matched scores are unchanged, including the LLaMA-based COCO R@1 values of 87.7/89.7 and ImageNet accuracy of 86.6%. v4 omits the Qwen2-specific Flickr30K results and v2's prediction-representation ablation entries, and replaces the loss-sensitivity findings with an optimum at alpha=0.5 under the revised protocol. Its improved reported VQA ranking follows ONE-PEACE's removal, not higher model scores.

T1.justification: v4's information-theoretic section reuses v2 Section 3's alignment decomposition, mutual-information/conditional-entropy objectives and alternating-gradient updates. No new formal assumptions, theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added. Loss notation changes and removal of the duplicated encoding equation do not establish new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction substantially redefine the contribution around a multimodal JEPA framework with an MoE predictor, replacing much of v2's hierarchical-world-model and knowledge-fusion emphasis. v4 also newly advertises an information-theoretic analysis demonstrating optimality. The broad efficiency and generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: v4 introduces representation-collapse and predictor-information explanations and reinterprets classification results as evidence for treating labels as another modality. v2 instead emphasizes complementary visual representations and hierarchical expert reasoning. The loss discussion shifts from favoring greater contrastive emphasis to equal weighting, and VQA discussion adds concatenation versus cross-attention considerations. The appendix limitations largely remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project-code link, explicitly specifies VQA feature concatenation and the selected alpha=0.5, and clarifies audio-baseline result provenance. Conversely, it removes Qwen-specific retrieval/ablation annotations and the explicit last-three-layer LoRA description. Most expert counts, gating, hidden sizes and dropout settings remain in Appendix B.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts centrally toward extending JEPA to multimodal alignment, with new discussion and citation of Assran et al.'s JEPA work. Additional citations include Qwen-VL, NExT-GPT, AnyGPT and Sphinx-X. Existing energy-based-model and representation-convergence references gain a larger conceptual role, although much of the dedicated related-work section is retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. Methodology precedes the theoretical discussion, related work moves after experiments, eight research questions organize evaluation, and appendices become Sections A–D. The duplicated image/text-encoding subsection is removed, and experimental narratives are substantially rewritten.

P2.justification: The original multi-panel alignment overview is replaced by a first-page JEPA schematic. VQA and LoRA tables move into the main text, the prediction-ablation table disappears, the two-curve sensitivity plot becomes a single alpha curve, and the efficiency bar chart becomes prose. Tables, captions and page composition are extensively reformatted; the architecture and similarity-matrix graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The reorganization, clearer loss-weight reporting and code link are useful. However, v4 leaves unreconciled label-alignment versus feature-fusion descriptions for unchanged ImageNet results, removes the stronger ONE-PEACE comparison while emphasizing second-best rankings, and claims theoretical optimality without adding a proof. These changes modestly weaken methodological clarity and claim support despite largely stable empirical evidence.
